record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Does every globally hyperbolic, maximally extended solution of the Einstein or Einstein-Maxwell equations on V = R x S3 contain a maximal hypersurface and both a big bang and a big crunch; equivalently, are there vacuum or Einstein-Maxwell solutions on R x S3 that cannot be foliated by constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces, even in the spatially homogeneous Bianchi IX case?

evidence.quote: Prove that every globally hyperbolic, maximally extended spacetime solution of the Einstein o:r Einstein-Maxwell equations on V = RxS3 contains a maximal hype:rsurface (and also both a big bang and big crunch). Are there any vacuum or Einstein-Maxwell solutions on Rx83 which cannot be foliated by CMC hypersurfaces? (This is a restatement of the previous question). artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V = \mathbb{R}\times S^3$ and consider a globally hyperbolic, maximally extended spacetime $(V,g)$ that solves either the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ or the Einstein–Maxwell equations on $V$. A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset V$ is called maximal if its mean curvature vanishes, and is said to have constant mean curvature (CMC) if its mean curvature is constant. A "big bang" (respectively "big crunch") refers to a past (respectively future) crushing singularity at which the mean curvature of CMC Cauchy surfaces tends to $+\infty$ (respectively $-\infty$).

(a) Prove that every globally hyperbolic, maximally extended solution of the Einstein, or Einstein–Maxwell, equations on $V=\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ contains a maximal Cauchy hypersurface and exhibits both a big bang and a big crunch.

(b) Equivalently, decide whether there exists any vacuum or Einstein–Maxwell solution on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ that cannot be globally foliated by constant-mean-curvature Cauchy hypersurfaces.

(c) Establish the same result in the special case of spatially homogeneous solutions of Bianchi type IX (i.e. spacetimes admitting a transitive isometric action of $SU(2)$ on the spatial slices $S^3$).
artifact.status_search_result: The spatially homogeneous Bianchi IX subcase has been largely settled: vacuum Bianchi IX cosmologies admit global CMC foliations and possess both an initial and final crushing singularity (work of Lin–Wald and subsequent authors on Bianchi IX dynamics). The general question for arbitrary globally hyperbolic maximally extended vacuum or Einstein–Maxwell solutions on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ — existence of a maximal slice, of big bang and big crunch, and CMC foliability — appears to remain open; no proof or counterexample in full generality is recorded in the literature returned.

status_evidence.title: Bianchi VIII and IX vacuum cosmologies: Almost every solution forms particle horizons
status_evidence.snippet: Generic Bianchi IX vacuum solutions admit a CMC foliation with mean curvature ranging over all of (-infty, infty), giving big bang and big crunch.
status_evidence.claim: Bianchi IX vacuum case is essentially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Kasner-like regions near crushing singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Bianchi IX Einstein flows are homogeneous CMC Einstein flows on S^3 with a crushing singularity.
status_evidence.claim: CMC foliations exist for Bianchi IX with crushing singularities.

status_evidence.title: CMC foliations and their conformal aspects
status_evidence.snippet: General existence of CMC foliations in globally hyperbolic spacetimes remains a subtle problem.
status_evidence.claim: The general CMC foliation question on R x S^3 is not settled.
